name: Weapons, Armor and Mounted Combat (Dark Ages)

pages.name: Weapons, Armor and Mounted Combat (Dark Ages)

text.content:
The core challenge and combat mechanics of Mind's Eye Theatre are unchanged in AD 1230, but the Dark Medieval's weaponry, armor, and battlefield conditions differ enormously from the modern game. This entry covers those deltas: medieval weapon and armor cards, two-weapon fighting, and mounted combat.

Armor

Armor grants extra health levels absorbed before the wearer takes damage; it does not stop non-physical harm (blood-boiling Thaumaturgy, etc.) and cannot be layered. Fixing damaged armor requires tools, time, and a Static Physical Challenge with Crafts.

Shields

A shield grants bonus Traits in hand-to-hand combat (requires at least one level of Melee to claim), cannot defend against rear attacks, and rules out a second weapon or any Two-Hand Requirement weapon. Used offensively, a shield counts as one Bonus Trait, keeps its Negative Traits, and inflicts one bashing health level. Shields are never concealable.

Etiquette of Arms and Armor

Wearing armor indoors, or carrying large weapons into certain quarters, is considered extremely rude unless the character's duties specifically require it — and doing so anyway can cause more trouble than the weapon is worth.

Two-Weapon Combinations

A character needs four levels of Melee to fight with a weapon in each hand. A second active off-hand weapon adds one Bonus Trait to the Physical Trait total (in addition to the dominant-hand weapon's own Bonus Traits), but only one Bonus Trait may be claimed from the off-hand weapon regardless of its own rating. Both weapons' Negative Traits still apply. The wielder chooses which weapon causes damage on a successful hit; if only one weapon's Special Ability was used to win the challenge (e.g., a dagger's Speed), that weapon deals the damage. A specialization in the exact combination used (e.g., "longsword and dagger," "two axes") adds one further Bonus Trait.

Mounted Combat

Controlling Steeds

Horses are innately afraid of vampires. Any Physical Challenge attempted from horseback is one Trait down on ties unless the rider has Feral Speech, two Traits of Animal Ken, or a ghouled mount. In combat, this penalty rises to two Traits (one negated by more than three Traits of Ride, or by riding a ghouled steed). A steed that takes lethal damage shies and must be brought back under control with a Physical Challenge (Ride as retest); failure risks bolting or unseating the rider.

Combat Effects

  • Ground-based Melee/Brawl attackers suffer a two-Trait penalty to strike a mounted target, unless using a long weapon like a spear.
  • A mounted fighter can only apply as many Ability Traits from a single Ability per combat sequence as she currently has in Ride (e.g., Melee 4/Ride 1 limits her to one Melee Trait while mounted).
  • Damage taken while mounted forces a Simple Test to stay in the saddle; failure means being thrown and suffering two levels of bashing damage.

Charging and Lances

A mounted charge adds two levels of damage to a successful strike but imposes a one-Trait penalty to hit, and charges resolve first in the turn. Lances require a charge to use properly (otherwise resolved as a spear) and require Ride x3 and Melee x3 to wield without penalty; an unskilled lancer takes one level of bashing damage per level of lethal damage inflicted and must win a Static Physical Challenge (versus the damage caused) to stay mounted.

Horse Archery and Trampling

Without an Archery specialization in Mounted shooting, mounted archery suffers a two-Trait penalty on ties (four if the horse moves faster than a trot). A trained war-horse can trample or kick for two levels of lethal damage once per turn as its own action; shields do not block this attack, and a failed trampling attempt leaves horse and rider two Traits down for the following turn.
